summary: Lobsang Tenpa works in Tibetology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history and archaeology. He earned a Master of Philosophy at Jawaharlal Nehru University, where he studied under supervisor Sharad K. Soni.

A scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Lobsang Tenzin studied at Drepung Monastery. He served as abbot at Gyume Tantric College (attested 1987), director of the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (1988–2001), and Chancellor of Sanchi University of Buddhist-Indic Studies.

A scholar in Tibetology and history and archaeology, Lobsang Yongdan studied at Kumbum Monastery and earned his PhD at the University of Cambridge under Hildegard Diemberger. He held postdoctoral posts at the Max Planck Institute for the History of Science and the University of Bonn.

A specialist in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Loden Sherab Dagyab studied at Drepung Monastery and under the 14th Dalai Lama, Trijang Rinpoche, and Ling Rinpoche. He directed Tibet House, New Delhi (1964–1966), and worked as a Tibetologist at the University of Bonn from 1966.
Lodrö Chökyi Sengé studied under Rangjung Rigpe Dorje and Kalu Rinpoche, and also taught Kalu Rinpoche.

Working in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Lodrö Sangpo studied under supervisor Ernst Steinkellner. He founded the Nitartha Institute in 1996 and served as a senior teacher at Gampo Abbey (attested 2008).

Lokesh Chandra was an Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology scholar. He earned a master's at the University of the Punjab and a PhD at Utrecht University under Jan Gonda. He directed the International Academy of Indian Culture (~1963–2022) and chaired the ICHR (~2014–2017).
Longlian was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Fazun starting in 1939 and under traditional teacher Nenghai Shi from circa 1941 to 1967.

Lore Sander works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She studied under Ernst Waldschmidt (~1962–1967) and held positions at the Museum of Asian Art (curator, 1987) and Free University of Berlin (lecturer, 1994).

Lori Meeks specializes in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She studied at Columbia University (BA) and Princeton University (PhD under Jacqueline I. Stone), later joining the University of Southern California in 2004 as Assistant Professor of Religious Studies.

Lorna Dewaraja specialized in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at the University of Ceylon and the University of London, she served as Associate Professor of History at the University of Ceylon and on the faculty of the University of Colombo.

Lothar Ledderose is a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology. He studied at Bonn, Heidelberg, Princeton, Harvard, Tokyo, and Cologne (Habilitation), and served as Professor at Heidelberg University (~1976–2010) and President of the Deutsche Morgenländische Gesellschaft (1978–1990).

A scholar of Sinology and archaeology, Lothar von Falkenhausen studied at Bonn, Peking University, Kyoto, and Harvard (PhD 1988). He became Full Professor at the University of California, Los Angeles in 1993, later serving as its Associate Director (2004–2011).

Louis Dumont worked in Indology and religious studies, studying under Marcel Mauss and Walther Schubring. He taught at the University of Oxford (1951–1955) and served as Directeur d'Études at the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences from 1955.

Louis Finot was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and archaeology who studied under Sylvain Lévi at the École des chartes. He served as Director of the École française d'Extrême-Orient (from 1898) and taught at the Collège de France (1920–1930).
Louis Gabaude is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies who held a post at the École française d'Extrême-Orient circa 1980.

Louis Gernet studied at the École Normale Supérieure (~1902–1905) and worked in history and archaeology. He held posts at the University of Algiers (~1917–1948) and the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1948–1962).

Louis H. Gray specialized in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. After completing degrees at Princeton and Columbia (PhD), he held academic posts at Princeton University (~1900–1902) and the University of Nebraska-Lincoln (Associate Professor of Philosophy, 1921).

Louis Havet was a linguistics scholar who studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Michel Bréal, Gaston Paris, and Abel Bergaigne. He served as professor and Latin philology department chair at the Collège de France from 1885 to 1925.

Louis Renou was a French Indologist and linguist who studied under Antoine Meillet and Jules Bloch. He held major posts at the University of Lyon (~1925–1937), the University of Paris/Sorbonne (~1937–1966), and the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1928–1966).
